mechanism_narrative: The current federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is inversely related to S&P 500 20-day forward returns; a lower value of FEDFUNDS predicts positive returns.
failure_condition: The average 20-day forward return when FEDFUNDS is below 1.5% is not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.0%, it indicates a strong labor market that supports corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE < 4.0%, the average 20-day forward return is not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When residential fixed investment (RSAFS) growth exceeds 0.5% monthly and housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1200 thousand units, it indicates a strong housing market that supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where RSAFS growth > 0.5% and HOUST > 1200, the average 20-day forward return is not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 2.5%, it signals a monetary tightening cycle that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS > 2.5%, the average 20-day forward return is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: The current housing starts (HOUST) is positively related to S&P 500 5-day forward returns; a higher HOUST value predicts positive returns.
failure_condition: The correlation between HOUST and SPX 5-day returns is not positive (i.e., correlation coefficient not significantly positive) or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1250 thousand units, it indicates a strong housing market that supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST > 1250, the average 60-day forward return is not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) growth exceeds 0.5% monthly and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) remains below 1.5%, it indicates a strong economy with accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: strong economy with accommodative monetary policy
failure_condition: In periods where INDPRO growth > 0.5% and FEDFUNDS < 1.5%, the average 20-day forward return is not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In labor market tightness regimes (defined by UNRATE < 4.0% and PAYEMS growth > 0.5% monthly), the S&P 500 forward returns are negative over the next 5 trading days due to rising inflation expectations and potential monetary tightening.
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE < 4.0% and PAYEMS growth > 0.5%, the average 5-day forward return is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
